speaker: Doctor
text: Can you describe what happens right before you become unresponsive, and how long these episodes typically last? Do you have any awareness of your surroundings during these events?

speaker: Patient
text: 7-year-old boy. The patient has been experiencing recurrent episodes lasting 3–4 minutes each of facial grimacing and staring over the past month. During these episodes, he is nonresponsive and does not recall them afterward. He reports a muddy taste in his mouth before the onset of these episodes. His brother witnessed him waking up, staring, and making hand gestures during one episode. The patient felt lethargic and confused afterwards.

speaker: Doctor
text: Does the patient have any history of head trauma, high fever, or neurological issues? I would also like to know if there is a family history of seizures. REQUEST TEST: EEG

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: The muddy taste suggests an aura, and the automatisms with post-ictal confusion point toward focal seizures, likely originating in the temporal lobe. I will review the EEG results to confirm epileptiform discharges in that region. REQUEST TEST: EEG_Results

speaker: Measurement

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical presentation of an olfactory aura, automatisms, and post-ictal confusion, combined with EEG findings of right temporal lobe spikes, strongly supports a diagnosis of focal impaired awareness seizures. Given the normal MRI, this is likely idiopathic or due to microscopic pathology, but the electrical evidence is definitive. DIAGNOSIS READY: Right Temporal Lobe Epilepsy
